translated_text: Prague, January 10, 36. Babūs, your letters took quite a while to reach me, but that made me all the more delighted. I spent a long time in the hotel, lying sick in my room, thinking of nothing. I was overjoyed to see you, more than anything. I never felt pained at having you with me in that moment. I certainly wouldn't have said much to you—just looked at you and felt happy. I will long for Zeinis for a long time to come. I look at the pictures almost every day and show them off. By the way, I've taken some other photos myself; you'll get them in the next letter. I've already been skiing again. I realized that I've really learned a lot. If possible, I'll go out again on Sunday because it's snowed beautifully here the last few days. By the way, in 14 days, Egge is going to Germany. I hope he has good weather too and that he can still get Sparmarks in Strasbourg. He's feeling quite good here at the moment, as he has a nice girlfriend who works at the film studio. He's really a different guy since then. Tomorrow I'll inquire again at Elekta Film about work. Things haven't progressed for me yet, but there's no rush. In any case, I'm also convinced that I shouldn't work for free if possible. But that also depends on the opportunity. I know that these are very rare, and that it's impossible without connections. But I just have to wait for that moment. I'm so looking forward to it.
